items.title: Matic Cues feature lets you just talk to your robot vacuum or point at a mess to clean
items.raw_content: Matic has added voice and gesture control to its robot vacuum and mop through a software update called Matic Cues. After testing both features, the short and sweet of it is that voice control is really good. Just say, “Hey Matic, vacuum the kitchen,” and Matic gets to work. There is no phone to unlock, app to open, or smart home intermediary involved. You speak directly to the robot, and it responds. Matic Cues understands commands in more than 70 spoken languages. The feature is rolling out to every existing Matic through an over-the-air software update and will be included on all new robots.

items.raw_content: Google’s official Pixelsnap charger with stand is down to $35, making the charging bundle that actually works with every Pixel 11 model – not just one – less expensive than buying just the charging puck by itself.

items.title: Gemini is getting over a dozen new connected apps – here’s the list
items.raw_content: AI assistants are at their most useful when they can connect to other aspects of your digital life, and Gemini is expanding its integrations with over a dozen new connected apps incoming including the likes of Ticketmaster, Angi, Zocdoc, and more.

items.title: Google’s Tensor G6 in Pixel 11 isn’t a 2nm smartphone chip after all
items.raw_content: It was rumored that Google’s new Tensor G6, debuting in the Pixel 11, would be the first smartphone chip using TSMC’s 2nm process, but it turns out that won’t be the case.

items.title: Pixel 11 moves the NFC antenna to the top of the phone for easier payments, Tap to Share
items.raw_content: In a nice quality-of-life change, Google says it has moved the NFC antenna on its Pixel 11 phones to the top of the device, making it easier and just more logical to do things such as make mobile payments or use the new “Tap to Share” feature.

items.title: Live from New York, it’s another awkward Pixel keynote
items.raw_content: Good morning. What a day yesterday — we had a huge Google hardware event , a total solar eclipse , a truly terrible AI album , and a couple of powerful , cheap AI models released that are sure to make Google sweat. Oh, and we’ve made it to 10 issues! As a reminder, Inbox is the tech newsletter you should be able to read in around 95 seconds. We cover the most important 9to5Google stories from the last couple of days along with a few highlights from around the web. We publish every Tuesday and Thursday, and if you like what you read, please subscribe .

items.title: This electric aircraft fire truck hits 50 mph in under 20 seconds
items.raw_content: The “world’s first” electric aircraft fire truck now has a 400 kW fast charger to keep it ready for emergencies at Dallas Love Field Airport.

items.title: Kia sold over 8,000 EV2s in just 3 months
items.raw_content: Kia’s entry-level electric SUV is already making a name for itself. In its first three full months, Kia sold over 8,000 EV2s as full-scale sales begin.

items.title: Ford recalls nearly 90,000 Mustang Mach-E EVs because part of the trim can fall off
items.raw_content: Ford is recalling 86,543 Mustang Mach-E models because a piece of glass trim on the rear side could fall off while driving.

items.title: Tesla pays Musk 2.5 million times more than average worker, even as profits drop
items.raw_content: A new report shows Elon Musk as the highest-compensated CEO, making as much money as 2,522,203 average Tesla workers in 2025. This happened as the Tesla CEO presided over a significant drop in profits which he was largely personally responsible for.

items.title: Volvo wants to help you save money on car insurance
items.raw_content: It may not be 15 minutes like Geico’s, but Volvo’s new Safety Coach app is designed to help you drive safely while also lowering your car insurance premiums.

items.title: IONNA just beat every major EV fast-charging network
items.raw_content: IONNA has been operating public fast chargers for less than two years, but EV drivers already rank it higher than every other eligible US fast-charging network.

items.title: Report says Porsche will end Taycan production by 2030, reversing course
items.raw_content: Porsche will end Taycan production by 2030, claims a German media report. The cancellation is interesting in the light of an interview just last month where the Porsche CEO said the model isn’t going anywhere.

items.title: Tesla Electric launches $35/month Powerwall whole-home backup lease
items.raw_content: Tesla is now renting out whole-home backup for about $35 a month in Texas. The catch: you lease two Powerwalls and sign up for Tesla Electric. Tesla Energy announced the new “Powerwall Lease” today, bundling the battery hardware with its own retail electricity business to push the effective monthly cost far below what a normal battery lease would run.

items.title: Genesis unveils the GV80 HEV, its first hybrid with an ‘EV-like’ drive and better efficiency
items.raw_content: Genesis revealed the GV80 HEV, its first hybrid vehicle. The GV80 HEV will go on sale next month with an all-new hybrid system that delivers an “EV-like” drive and roughly a 25% improvement in fuel efficiency.

items.title: Tesla defeats Sweden’s IF Metall union after 1,021-day strike
items.raw_content: Sweden’s largest industrial union, IF Metall, is calling off its strike against Tesla after 1,021 days, the longest labor conflict in modern Swedish history. The union says it’s stopping because Tesla bought out every one of its striking members, leaving the walkout with nothing left to withhold. The dispute started in October 2023 over a single demand: that Tesla sign a Swedish collective bargaining agreement for its mechanics. Nearly three years later, Tesla still hasn’t signed one. And now the union is standing down.

items.title: Volkswagen’s new electric camper van turns the ID. Buzz into a home on wheels
items.raw_content: Volkswagen is giving people what they want — an all-electric, fully fledged camper van that can be assembled in minutes. The ID. California Cruise is coming as the first all-electric California camper.

items.title: Urban Arrow enters the longtail cargo e-bike market in US with its new Breeze
items.raw_content: Urban Arrow has spent the last 14 years building a reputation around front-loading cargo bikes, becoming one of the biggest names in the family cargo bike world. Now the Dutch company is branching out into an entirely new category with the launch of the Urban Arrow Breeze, bringing its first-ever longtail electric cargo bike to the North American market.

items.title: Rivian’s 2027 R1S adds captain’s chairs, its most-requested feature
items.raw_content: Rivian is rolling out its 2027 model year R1S and R1T, and the headline change is one owners have been asking for since day one: second-row captain’s chairs on the R1S. The automaker calls it the single most-requested feature since the R1S launched. It arrives alongside a simplified trim structure, a new standard wheel for the R1T, a new paint color, and higher starting prices across the board.

items.title: Ford’s EV pickup is almost here, promising much more than an affordable price tag
items.raw_content: The Ford Fathom will go on sale in early 2027, starting at $28,350. Ford said the electric pickup is on track to go into production at its Louisville Assembly plant in Q1 2027.

items.title: Rivian’s long-delayed ALSO e-bike is only delayed a little bit longer
items.raw_content: The wait for Rivian’s first electric bike just got a little bit shorter. After months of delays, ALSO has informed reservation holders that they’ll finally be able to place pre-orders for the company’s highly anticipated TM-B electric bike starting August 18. It’s welcome news for the unknown number of people who put down reservations, though it’s hard to ignore just how far the timeline has slipped.

items.title: First Fuel Loading Begins at Tianwan Unit 7 — CNNC Implants the 'Energy Heart' of a 900MW-Plus Nuclear Base
items.raw_content: On August 12, the first fuel assembly was precisely loaded into the reactor core of Tianwan Nuclear Power Plant Unit 7, marking the start of first fuel loading for the largest nuclear base in the world by installed and under-construction capacity. The China-Russia flagship project will see Units 7 and 8 enter commercial operation in 2026 and 2027.

items.title: WeChat's Xiaowei Agent Runs on WeLM — a Sparse MoE Model Quietly Growing to 617 Billion Parameters
items.raw_content: WeChat has started gray-testing Xiaowei, a native AI assistant embedded inside the app, powered by WeLM, the WeChat AI team's long-developed large language model. WeLM has moved to sparse MoE architecture, with a 617-billion-parameter version activating just 23 billion per token, and the team is exploring Hidden Decoding as a new scaling direction.

items.title: Nanjing University and Renshine Publish Meter-Scale Perovskite Modules in Nature — 22% Certified Efficiency With Field-Proven Gains Over Silicon
items.raw_content: A Nanjing University team led by Xiao Ke and Hairen Tan, working with Renshine's industrialization team, has published in Nature a lead-carboxylate passivation strategy that yields 22.0% certified full-area efficiency on 0.72m2 perovskite solar modules, passing IEC61215/IEC61730 reliability testing and outperforming co-located TOPCon silicon modules in real field generation.

items.title: Shunwei and CATL-Backed Wangqian Bet on NOUSBOT to Mass-Produce the World's Smallest Screws by the Millions

The company aims to lift annual capacity from 3 million to 10 million screws by year-end.

items.title: China's First Commercial Supercritical CO2 Closed-Loop Geothermal Project Turns the Earth into a Rechargeable Battery
items.raw_content: Huaneng engineers in Zhengzhou drilled a 2,500-meter well and circulated supercritical CO2 instead of water to extract geothermal heat, China's first commissioned closed-loop demonstration project. CO2 in at 8 degrees Celsius returns at 22 degrees, cutting pumping loss 10% and lifting heat-extraction capacity about 20%.

items.title: WPS Quietly Launches Lingxi Pro, an AI-Native Office Agent That Turns Skills into Editable Documents
items.raw_content: Kingsoft's WPS has quietly launched Lingxi Pro, a standalone AI-native office agent that makes AI the first entry point instead of a document feature.
